newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Dell rally spills into options.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Dell rally spills into options.

text.p: Investors scrambled to buy Dell Computer Corp calls to play a quick pop in the stock that was driven by solid earnings, a stock split and some positive brokerage comments, traders said Wednesday.
By 1440 CST/2040 GMT, the computer maker's stock was ahead 3-5/8 at 92-1/4, well off its session high of 93-1/2, which was an all-time peak.
Volume was heavy at roughly 6.45 million shares.
"We've been getting a lot of people trying to buy it," one options trader said. "Everybody's trying to jump on the bandwagon."
He said some investors were requesting calls with a 100 strike price, but the highest existing strike is 95 and those were only available in the December, January and February expirations.
Philadelphia Stock Exchange may add 100 strike prices after the close of trading Wednesday. No new strikes would be added to the November series, which expires Friday.
The trader added that most investors were playing for a quick pop in the stock, which was why the bulk of the options activity was in the November 90 calls.
November 90 call traded nearly 4,000 contracts and was up 15/16 at 2-15/16. Traders said volatility surged to about 52.

"Whether (volatilities) will come back, my guess is the way the stock's acting, they're probably going to hang in there for a day or two at least at these levels," said Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN.
He said the bulk of the action was straight buying.
"To me it looks like there are real speculative buyers looking for the stock to go even higher," he said.
The November 85 call traded about 2,100 contracts and the December 90 and 95 calls each traded more than 1,400.
On the put side, the November 90 traded about 1,500 contracts and the December 75 traded 1,055.
The trader said the bulk of the activity, in the November 90 calls and puts, and the December 90 and 95 calls, suggested investors were positioning themselves for a quick rally.
"It's the old axiom that once a stock gets into the 90's, it's going to go over 100," he said. "So a lot of people are playing it."
Beyond the December series, the busiest Dell option was the February 85 put, which traded about 525 contracts. The January 90 call traded nearly 500 contracts.
Tuesday, Dell said it approved a two-for-one stock split payable Dec 6 to shareholders of record Nov 25.
It also reported third quarter profits of $1.52 a share before a $0.04 per share charge, compared with $0.75 a share in the year-ago quarter.
Bear Stearns upgraded its rating on Dell to buy from attractive and raised its fiscal 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates on Wednesday.
Prudential Securities also raised its fiscal 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates, a source at the brokerage house said. --Gregory Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
